input.quote: each Party will carry and maintain, at its own expense, insurance coverage of the kind and with liability limits that, at a minimum, satisfy the requirements of Section 12.3.2, to protect itself and the other Party against any claims or liabilities that may arise from the conduct of the Clinical Trials and all other rights and obligations hereunder with insurers with a minimum "A-" A.M. Best rating.
input.rationale: Section 12.3 contains a full, mutual insurance regime that binds SFJ as well as PB: commercial general liability (12.3.2.1), umbrella excess liability (12.3.2.2), clinical trials liability (12.3.2.3), professional liability for subcontractors/Permitted Third Parties providing professional services (12.3.2.4) and product liability (12.3.4), each set at the greater of the Applicable Law minimum or the stated limit, with "A-" A.M. Best-rated insurers, primary and non-contributing cover, additional-insured status for us on clinical trial liability, tail coverage after termination, prior notice of cancellation/material change, an express statement that insurance does not cap liability, a flow-down requiring subcontractors to be insured, and certificates of insurance on written request. That satisfies the preferred position on coverage types and certificate mechanics; the specific limits are redacted ([***]) so amounts cannot be verified from the face of the document, and there is no dedicated cyber/privacy line (personal data handling is instead addressed in Article 11). These are minor sub-elements in a co-development/clinical trial agreement rather than a hosting or data-processing engagement, and are noted rather than redlined; the obligation is mutual and confers a benefit on us as an insured party, so no change is proposed.
